avoid_supplements.name: Warfarin (if concurrent use)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Additive anticoagulant effect increases bleeding risk; enoxaparin and warfarin have overlapping mechanisms
avoid_supplements.action: Do not combine without explicit clinical indication and close INR monitoring; transition carefully if switching anticoagulants

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation and may potentiate anticoagulant effect, increasing bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discontinue ginkgo at least 2 weeks before enoxaparin or if already on therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Garlic (high-dose supplements)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet function and may increase bleeding risk when combined with anticoagulants
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid high-dose garlic supplements; dietary garlic in normal amounts is generally acceptable

avoid_supplements.name: Feverfew
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Inhibits platelet aggregation and thromboxane synthesis, compounding anticoagulant effects
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; counsel patient to discontinue before enoxaparin therapy

avoid_supplements.name: Dong quai
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Contains coumarin-like compounds that enhance anticoagulation and increase bleeding risk
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; discontinue supplement prior to enoxaparin initiation

caution_supplements.name: Fish oil (omega-3 fatty acids)
caution_supplements.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects; may slightly increase bleeding risk at very high doses (>3g/day)
caution_supplements.action: Monitor for signs of bleeding; limit to ≤3g/day or monitor closely if higher doses used

caution_supplements.name: Turmeric/Curcumin
caution_supplements.mechanism: May have mild antiplatelet and anti-inflammatory properties at high doses
caution_supplements.action: Counsel patient to avoid excessive supplementation; dietary amounts are safe

caution_supplements.name: Cranberry supplements
caution_supplements.mechanism: Possible mild interaction through polyphenol content affecting coagulation; evidence is weak
caution_supplements.action: Monitor INR/PT if concurrent use; cranberry juice in normal amounts is generally safe

avoid_foods.name: High-dose vitamin K foods (if unstable dosing)
avoid_foods.mechanism: Vitamin K antagonizes anticoagulant effect; excessive intake may reduce enoxaparin efficacy indirectly by affecting overall coagulation balance
avoid_foods.action: Maintain consistent vitamin K intake from foods like leafy greens; avoid sudden increases or decreases

caution_foods.name: Leafy green vegetables (spinach, kale, broccoli)
caution_foods.mechanism: Contain vitamin K which affects coagulation; inconsistent intake may alter hemostasis balance
caution_foods.action: Consume in consistent amounts; no need to restrict but maintain dietary stability

caution_foods.name: Alcohol (moderate-to-heavy consumption)
caution_foods.mechanism: Chronic heavy alcohol use impairs coagulation and increases bleeding risk; acute use may potentiate anticoagulation
caution_foods.action: Counsel patient to limit alcohol to ≤1-2 drinks daily; avoid binge drinking

caution_foods.name: Ginger (culinary amounts)
caution_foods.mechanism: Mild antiplatelet effects at high supplemental doses; normal dietary use is minimal risk
caution_foods.action: Dietary ginger is acceptable; avoid concentrated ginger supplements or excessive amounts

monitoring_notes: Enoxaparin is a parenteral anticoagulant with no significant hepatic metabolism; interactions are primarily related to additive anticoagulant/antiplatelet effects. Monitor for signs of bleeding (petechiae, hematuria, GI bleeding, excessive bruising) and assess renal function periodically, as enoxaparin is renally cleared.
